outcome: No proof, disproof, or newly settled case of Vojta's general conjecture on heights of points on algebraic varieties over algebraic number fields has appeared since 26 January 2024; all located work addresses variants (the abc-conjecture analogue over function fields, algebraic tori, or entire curves in toric varieties via Nevanlinna theory) or narrow K-stability-based sufficient conditions that do not amount to a settled case of the stated height-inequality conjecture, and no AI involvement was found anywhere in this area.
summary: Vojta's conjecture, as stated in the frozen Wikipedia bullet, is the general height-inequality conjecture for points on algebraic varieties over algebraic number fields (Vojta, 1987), a broad generalization encompassing Roth's theorem, Mordell/Faltings, and the abc conjecture as special cases. I ran targeted searches for any proof, disproof, or newly-settled case since 26 January 2024 and found only work on adjacent but distinct statements: (1) arXiv:2410.19395 (Oct 2024, updated Feb 2026) proves 'Vojta's abc conjecture' for entire curves in toric varieties highly ramified over the boundary — this is the Nevanlinna-theoretic complex-analytic analogue (entire curves, not rational/integral points over number fields), a genuinely different mathematical object sharing only the name; (2) the ScienceDirect/JPAA 2025 paper (an updated version of arXiv:2106.15881, originally 2021) proves the abc-analogue for algebraic tori over function fields, not number fields; (3) the Monatshefte 2024 GCD-inequality paper is explicitly 'inspired by' the conjecture rather than a proof of any of its cases; (4) arXiv:2401.01428 (Jan 2024, essentially at the window boundary) uses K-stability of Q-Fano varieties to exhibit settings (a torus-invariant divisor on toric Fano varieties) where Vojta's conjecture's predicted inequality holds — this is a narrow sufficient-condition/special-setting result on toric varieties, arguably closer to a case but still a restricted geometric class rather than a case that changes what a careful reader would write about the general conjecture, and it is dated essentially at the frozen revision's timestamp with no indication of being later strengthened; (5) arXiv:2508.11888 (Aug 2025, updated Nov/Dec 2025) reorganizes Vojta's own 1991 proof of the Mordell conjecture (Faltings' theorem) using Arakelov geometry and a newer arithmetic Siu inequality — this is a re-proof of an already-known special case (abelian/curves case, settled by Faltings 1991, itself predating the window by decades), not new progress on the conjecture. The Wikipedia article on Vojta's conjecture itself does not mention any post-2024 developments; its only cited resolved special case remains Faltings' 1991 theorem for abelian varieties, which long predates the window. No source anywhere in this search mentioned AI, machine learning, or any AI system in connection with Vojta's conjecture; the only AI-mathematics story that surfaced in these searches (an AI-found counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture) is an unrelated problem that a naive keyword search could conflate with this one. I therefore agree with the triage's 'none' verdict and its classification of all found items as variants rather than cases.
competing_reading: arXiv:2401.01428's K-stability result could be argued to be a genuine 'case' of Vojta's conjecture (a restriction to toric Fano varieties with a specific divisor) rather than a 'related problem,' which under §3.1 would warrant `partial` status with `resolution_direction: confirmed`. I did not classify it this way because (a) it is dated January 2, 2024, essentially indistinguishable from the frozen revision's timestamp of January 26, 2024, so even if counted it contributes negligible information about post-window progress, and (b) from the abstract alone it is unclear whether it establishes new cases or surveys/re-derives previously known settings connecting K-stability to the conjecture; I could not access the full text to confirm the precise scope of what is newly proved.
what_would_settle_it: Reading the full text of arXiv:2401.01428 to determine precisely which toric Fano varieties and divisors it newly establishes the conjecture for, and whether any of that is dated after 26 January 2024 (e.g., in a later arXiv revision) or was already known before the paper. Also, a direct search of Paul Vojta's own publication list and any survey articles or ICM-type reports post-2024 on Diophantine approximation would help confirm no case has been missed.
